body.statement: Among supports with \(\kappa_0(S)=\eta(S)=0\), characterize exactly those \(S\) for which \(\operatorname{rank}M_\theta=Q_S\) for every \(\theta\in\Theta_S\), and for every remaining support construct a strictly positive compatible one-parameter family crossing the determinantal exceptional locus while keeping support \(S\) fixed.
body.justification: Generic feasibility does not certify completeness at the actual law, so the uniform frontier is the principal open content beyond the generic rank theorem.
body.gap: Allman, Matias, and Rhodes separate generic from global identifiability for latent product models, but no support-only classification is available for fortified proximal pairing matrices.
body.consumer: A uniform-support certificate would justify completeness without an unobservable law-specific rank premise; an exceptional-family certificate would identify where actual-law diagnostics remain indispensable.
